p1: Long ago, Isaiah told the people what Heavenly Father said. He gave them happy words: “Arise, shine; for your light has come!”
Think of a dark night. Then the sun comes up. People wake up and get up!
That is the picture Isaiah used. He told them to get up and shine. The Lord’s bright goodness was shining on them!
p2: Isaiah said darkness covered the earth, but the Lord would shine on His people. People from far lands, even kings, would come to that light. Jesus is that light! He said, “I am the light of the world.”
When you are kind, others can see Jesus’s light in you. Tomorrow when you wake, get up and shine!
old: A long time ago, Heavenly Father had a helper named Isaiah. A helper like that is called a prophet, and a prophet tells people what Heavenly Father wants them to know. Isaiah's people were sad. They had been taken far away from home, and their city was broken, and some of them had stopped listening to Heavenly Father. Their days felt dark, the way a room feels when the curtains are shut tight.

So Isaiah said something surprising. "Get up! Shine! Your light has come!" He did not mean a candle. The light Isaiah was talking about is Jesus. When Isaiah said the world was dark, he meant people were sad and doing wrong things. And when he said light, he meant Jesus coming to make it all better, the way the sun comes up slow and warm over a dark hill.

Isaiah said people from far, far away, even kings, would come walking toward that light. That is because everybody wants to be where it is warm and bright and safe. And when Jesus puts His light in you, you shine too, so other people can see the good that is in you.
Isaiah also said that one day we will not need the sun in the daytime or the moon at night. Jesus Himself will be our light, always on, never going out. And nobody will be sad anymore.
Your little nightlight will go dark someday. That light never will. Jesus is close to you tonight, even in the dark. Sleep now.
